title: Bean scopes
context: What are the bean scopes in Spring?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `singleton`, the default, creates one instance per container. `prototype` creates a new instance each time the bean is requested. In web apps, `request` gives one per HTTP request, `session` one per user session, and `application` one per ServletContext. `websocket` gives one per WebSocket session. Singletons are created at startup, while prototypes are created on demand, and the container does not manage their destruction.

points.title: Singleton default
points.why: Most beans are singletons, so their state is shared across all requests.

points.title: Prototype cleanup
points.why: The container doesn't call destroy for prototype beans, so close them yourself.
